text:
The first overall pick is the biggest story in Toronto, and right now it's about his minutes. Gavin McKenna plays 13:57 a night, and Jim Hiller hasn't used him in overtime; Daily Faceoff Toronto reported Hiller "wants to make sure Gavin McKenna is 'ready'" first. Sportsnet asked "How should Maple Leafs handle Gavin McKenna?" and The New York Times asked why he isn't playing in overtime.

The 18-year-old's line is solid for his role: 6 goals and 14 points in 24 games, 7 on the power play. His skating jumps out, in the 97th percentile for top speed per NHL EDGE. His finishing is a little ahead of his chances, 6 goals on 4.6 expected goals (the quality of his shots).

The case for caution is at five on five, where Toronto gets only 41.7% of the expected goals with him on, about 6 points worse than without him. For context, forwards picked first to third since 2005 scored a median 0.55 points a game in their first full season; Connor Bedard and Macklin Celebrini both did 0.90. Watch whether his ice time moves.
